utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll continue with the questions this morning. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that your first name is Vukmir. Are you known by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vule. That is my nickname, Vule.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a man by the name of Zoran Djurisic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Djurisic. It's a policeman from the Decani OUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what sort of job did he do at the Decani OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a traffic policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to take you back to your testimony of yesterday. You during the course of questions by my learned colleague you referred to an incident in the village of Istinic concerning the voluntary hand-over of weapons. Do you recall speaking about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said, if I remember correctly, that this incident took place sometime in September of 1998?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In relation to this incident, you said that you had -- and this is at transcript page 13263 -- that you had confirmed operational information that in Istinic village, Decani municipality, there were a lot of refugees from Decani and other villages and that there was a great concentration of civilians, women, children, the elderly there. And you said that your assessment was that there were between 15- to 20.000 people gathered there at the time. Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And on the same page you said that the reason for the large concentration of civilians in Istinic at the time was that civilians wanted to avoid being caught in cross-fire between the KLA and the police in the general area of the municipalities of Djakovica and Decani in the village of Jablanica and so on and so forth. Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The village of Jablanica, where is that located?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jablanica village is located in the territory of the Djakovica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you are saying, sir, if I understand your evidence correctly, that this large concentration of civilians, this 15- to 20.000 people that had gathered in Istinic, were not only from Decani but they also came from the municipality of Djakovica, from the general area of the village of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: At the time that this large number of civilians concentrated or gathered there in Istinic village, the police was carrying a large scale action in the general areas of Jablanica and also in the Decani municipality in the area of Glodjane; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the aim of this action was to disarm and neutralise the KLA in those areas?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in addition to having information about there being a large number of civilian in Istinic, you also had information that there was KLA presence there and that there were -- they had weapons there in that village?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that in September when this large group of civilians was in Istinic, General Djordjevic was in the area of your OUP at the time, and you said that he had come to acquaint himself with the overall situation in the field as well as the work of the Ministry of the Interior and its members and whether they conducted themselves properly and in a fashion prescribed by the law. Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said that you had informed him about the situation in Istinic and you had proposed to tackle this problem of the fact that there were so many refugees there in a peaceful manner?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If this issue of the fact that there were weapons in Istinic wasn't tackled in a peaceful manner, sir, isn't it correct that the police would have proceeded to -- I see you are making signs to your -- are you not receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I hear it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'll go back to repeat my question again. Sir, you said that you had proposed to tackle the problem of the fact that there were weapons there and a large number of civilians in a peaceful manner. The alternative to this issue not being resolved in a peaceful manner would have been for the police to go in and confront the KLA and there would have been civilian casualties; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course that was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you proposed to -- you presented this issue to General Djordjevic, didn't you also tell him that if the police operation, which was underway in the general area of Decani was to be carried out as planned, and this village was, in fact, attacked by the police because the terrorists were entrenched there, they would offer fierce resistance and civilians would suffer? Didn't you also say that to him?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't tell him that. I just told him that the estimate was that the number of the population that was there was as mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you didn't tell him that if the police action that was planned was carried out, there would be civilian casualties? You don't recall telling him that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to show you, sir, the transcript of the testimony of General Djordjevic who testified in these proceedings, and he spoke about this incident, and maybe that refreshes your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we can go to transcript page 9622, and if that can be displayed on the screen. And this is the transcript of the 4th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, while that is being displayed and in order not to lose time I'll read the passage to you. Mr. Djordjevic was asked -- I'm looking for page 9622. Mr. Djordjevic was asked: "Did you have any direct experience or were you in the village of Istinic at the time, if so, please tell us." And he says, if I'm not wrong, this is on the 10th of December, actually, so in mid-September -- 10th of September, actually mid-September. Yeah, I see the passage is there. "At that time we had certain intelligence that in the area there were civilians, and we were discussing how to return them to their homes because there were people from some other villages as well. I personally wasn't present there, but I was there towards the end of September when a large-scale operation was being carried out in the area from Jablanica and Glodjane which were known to be strongholds of terrorists." And if I scroll down it says: "At the time I was in the area of the secretariats of Pec and Djakovica, rather, the municipal secretariat of Decani. I'm talking about the time when one of these final operations was in progress. I was there with the head of the section of the interior, Mircic, who informed me that he had intelligence about tens of thousands of civilians who were there in Istinic and who had come from some 20-odd villages in the area. These villagers found shelter there because of the operation that was ongoing and probably as instructed by the terrorist organisations. He told me that if all these actions were to be carried through as planned and since the village of Istinic was sealed off, one would expect that the terrorists would put up fierce resistance in the area. And his statement was, given that he was quite familiar with the situation there, that in the clashes and neutralisations of their stronghold, the result -- they might result in a large number of civilian casualties." Does that refresh your recollection of the discussion you had with General Djordjevic in relation to this operation?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, because a lot of time has passed, one cannot remember everything. That was exactly what the conversation was about these circumstances. I remember every sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you did have information that a police operation was underway; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have the information that the police action was underway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you had information that a large-scale police operation was underway in Jablanica and the general area of Decani, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you also knew that if this action continued, the village of Istinic would also be targeted since the KLA was also present there?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an estimate. That was what was estimated at the time that it would be like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just so I understand your answer to be that, yes, you had this information that it was estimated that this is how the operation would continue, this village would be attacked since the KLA was there and this was an operation targeting the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, yesterday when we were talking about police operations in your area and we went over this quite a bit towards the end of the session yesterday, you insisted repeatedly that you had no information about any actions that were carried out in your municipality. You, in fact, said you heard shots, you heard from a distance but you did not know about any actions carried out in your municipality. Do you recall saying that yesterday when I was asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have firsthand information about the areas where the operations were carried out and what operations these were. Because there were operations underway everywhere in the field, in the entire territory of the municipality, so to speak, so that was no secret. So that no one would know when one heard detonations and you heard heavy machine-gun fire, one could assume what was going on and in which area. But nobody directly informed me about where certain operations were carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But in this specific instance that we are looking at Istinic, you yourself proposed to General Djordjevic that this situation of the weapons in Istinic be resolved in a peaceful manner, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the concentration of the population was so great, that was the only plan we had, and we really tried to resolve it in a peaceful manner because there was a large number of civilians concentrated there, and there was the KLA as well. They were keeping the population there in their trenches and on their barricades, so we supposed that if they were to attack the police or if there was to be a conflict with the police, that the consequences would be disastrous for the population.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you made this proposal because you knew there was an action underway and that Istinic would be attacked given that KLA presence was -- there were KLA presence there, no? You knew that much of what was going on in Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that was not an action carried out in Decani. That's another area. The action was carried out in Djakovica. So it's doubtful whether the action would be carried out in Istinic or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, earlier I asked you whether this large-scale police action was also being carried out in the general area of Decani and Glodjani, and you said yes. Are you now telling me that there was no action being carried out in Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, but not in Decani itself but just in the general area of Decani. It was not carried out in the village of Decani. We had no action there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I'm not suggesting that, sir, we are speaking about the general area of Decani municipality, not the village of Decani, so can we agree, sir, that you had did have information that there was this action and that Istinic would be next given that the KLA was there, it was one of the targets of this action by the police?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware that one of the targets or one of the goals of the action was that and that the action would continue in that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But it is something that you expected and that is why you raised this issue with General Djordjevic when he came to see you in Decani OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told him what the intelligence was, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I just showed you earlier the transcript of the testimony of General Djordjevic where he says that you advised him that if the action was carried out as planned, there would be civilian casualties. Doesn't that show, sir, that you knew that Istinic was a potential target of this police action that was being carried out in Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that an action was planned with Istinic being its target. I just knew that in the wider area of Jablanica and other places within Djakovica municipality there were actions underway. You could hear the shots. You could hear the combat activity that was underway. But I wasn't aware of any plan. Probably there was a plan. That was necessary in order for the action to be taken out, but I wasn't aware that an action was planned for the village of Istinic. I simply said that there was a possibility for an action there and that there was a potential of large number of victims, casualties being inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Earlier when I showed you the testimony of General Djordjevic, you said that you remember that conversation, that it was like that in every word; do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I never said that an action was imminent. I said if there was an action, I never said that I knew about any action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are saying you knew that there was a police action in Djakovica municipality and in the wider area of Jablanica and you could hear the shots from Decani town, that this was going on in Djakovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And from the area of Glodjani.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And Glodjani is in which municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is within the municipality of Decani. That is very close to Jablanica, so it's bordering the area of the municipality of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So you had information that in these two general areas there were police actions. Now, you've told us that you propose to tackle this problem in a peaceful manner. Where did this discussion take place with General Djordjevic, this discussion about the Istinic situation?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have information about actions in the area of Jablanica and Glodjani. And could you please repeat your question concerning General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we seem to either be having a translation issue here or we are misunderstanding each other. I'm putting to you that you you knew that there was a general police action in the wider area of Jablanica in Djakovica municipality and in the general area of Glodjani in the Decani municipality? Is that correct, that you knew that was going on?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that, and I'm not sure what is your foundation for this claim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My foundation is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Someone keeps turning off my headphone, I would request I don't know why that's happening, if that could stop because I lose the interpretation every time that happens.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, my foundation is my answer to -- your answer to my question earlier when I asked you whether there was a police action going on underway in Jablanica and Glodjani and you said, yes, that is my foundation. I asked you at the time that this large number of civilians concentrated and gathered there in Istinic village, the police was carrying out a large-scale action in the general area of Jablanica also in the Djakovica area, and in Glodjani, correct, and you said that is right; do you recall giving that answer just this morning?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about this, but I wasn't informed by anybody, and I had no plan. I never participated in drafting of any plan. I simply heard detonations, I heard that combat activities were underway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not putting to you that you participated in the drafting of a plan, I'm just trying to ascertain your knowledge about what was going on in the municipality, that is all that I'm trying to establish here, and your knowledge. I'm speaking about your specific knowledge about the fact that there was this large-scale operation going on.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that. It was only the staff and the secretariat in that region that knew about this. I didn't know about this. I could only assume on the basis of the direction from which I could hear shots being fired and detonations, so I could assume there was an action going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We seem to be going in circles, sir, with this topic really. Earlier today I asked you about this and you said that that was correct, this action was going on, and when I asked you whether the aim was to neutralise and disarm the KLA, you said that was right. And now you are saying you did not know about that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said I knew about it. I said I heard about this. I said it was underway on the basis of my assumption because I knew this area very well, and I could recognise the directions from which the detonations could be heard, so I could immediately assume where the combat was ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on from this. And so you proposed to General Djordjevic that the issue of the disarming of Istinic be carried out in a peaceful manner, that is, without police intervention in order for there not to be civilian casualties; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I had asked earlier whether -- where the discussion with General Djordjevic had taken place?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was sometime in the course of 1998, whether it was in September, this is as much as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My question was at line 17 - I see it's been incorrectly transcribed - was where the discussion with General Djordjevic has taken place. Was this at the premises of your OUP, or was -- did this discussion take place somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in the office of the OUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And that would have been in Decani town?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the OUP seat was in the town of Decani.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said that when the discussion took place, also present there was the municipal president, and I believe you said his name was Milivoj Djurkovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you told us that General Djordjevic agreed with your proposal and that you followed it up?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You also indicated yesterday that a person with some standing in the community, I believe you said his name was Elis Bajlaj [phoen] was sent to Istinic to negotiate this hand-over of weapons -- peaceful hand-over of weapons?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And while these negotiations were ongoing there was no police action against Istinic, correct, during the time that this person was there negotiating with the villagers? The police did not intervene?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the police did not interfere. Obviously if there was any action underway, we could not have negotiated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And later this person came back and returned and told you that the KLA had agreed to voluntarily hand over weapons and they withdrew from the village?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came back, as I said, and informed us that an agreement had been made with all the respected renowned villagers of Albanian nationality from all the villages in the area, so also in respect of the population that came there from the surrounding villages. They agreed that they would hand over the weapons and we could implement our proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you've told us, and we don't need to go into the details again, that this, in fact, was done, that there was a voluntarily -- the weapons were voluntarily handed over and that you, General Djordjevic, and also Zoran Andjelkovic later went to the village; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went to the village. There was also Milivoj Djurkovic, the municipal president.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And [Microphone not activated] ... of this agreement that was reached, the police operation that was expected to be launched or carried out against Istinic did not happen? Following this hand-over, there was no police action against Istinic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there wasn't any police action in Istinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So the police action, in fact, ended there with that agreement?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean. There was never any police action in Istinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that, sir. Sir, I want to move on to a different topic, and we are going to move on now to 1999. You were asked whether in 1999 ethnic Albanians, Serbs, and Montenegrins left the territory of Decani, and you said, and this is at transcript page 13289 and continues on the next page, that: "Yes, that's a well known fact that both the Serbs and Montenegrins and ethnic Albanians would leave the territory of Decani and the municipality of Decani because they feared for themselves, they were worried about the fate of their families. Serbs mostly left in the direction of Serbia or Montenegro, whereas Albanians would also leave in the direction of Montenegro, Macedonia, or Albania." Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You were also asked, and this is on page 13290: "... did you see refugees from other areas in Kosovo and Metohija who were possibly passing through the territory of Decani?" And you said "Yes, we can say that from Pec through Istok and Klina these areas are connected by a road leading to Djakovica, and I was in a position to see long convoys of people, Albanians." Do you recall giving that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall saying that, and that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately when you began seeing this large convoys of Albanian going through Decani municipality from the areas of Pec and Istok, Klina that you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that precisely, which month it was. Probably it was at the beginning of the NATO bombing campaign, so after the 24th of March and further on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you see these large convoys of refugees from the beginning of the NATO bombing throughout the next month, or was there a period when this flow was more intense, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, we can't say that there were long convoys all the time, but from time to time you could see some convoys. I can't say that they were endless, but occasionally, you could see some convoys somewhere. Sometimes they were shorter, sometimes they were longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you speak about long convoys, just so we have a better idea, approximately how large were these convoys are we talking about? Hundreds of people, thousands of people? How many people would you see in these convoys that were going through Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't talk about the number of people. They were all driving their cars or tractors, so we could say approximately 100 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you would see groups of 100 people going through your municipality, and they would be heading in which direction?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went in the direction of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was this something that you personally observed while you were out on the road in Decani municipality, these convoys of people?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them personally. I even spoke to them. I asked why they moved out, where from, and where they were heading, and they would answer that because of the new security situation, because of the propaganda that was being spread by the KLA and because of the orders that they also had, they had to leave their villages and they were told that they couldn't be protected anymore from the Serbian forces and that they couldn't guarantee for their lives anymore. So this was already said. They were also informed that they could find themselves in a cross-fire between the KLA and NATO bombing because NATO continuously bombed the area of Decani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting my learned colleague. I just want to make sure that we have something in the transcript. In line 16 we have something that the witness never said in Serbian, so could we please clarify this so that where the orders are mentioned, the orders that I had, so this is something that he never actually said in Serbian, so I just want to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You notice the position, Ms. Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the passage in question is the one that said they couldn't be protected anymore from Serbian forces and they couldn't guarantee for their lives anymore. I presume that's the passage in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I don't see -- oh, because of the orders that I also had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, just to go back to your answer and to clarify it. You said, when we were talking about this convoys of people, you said they would answer that because of the new security situation, because of the propaganda that was being spread by the KLA, and because of the orders that I also had they had to leave their villages; is that what you meant to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I never mentioned orders that I had. This is not in conformity with the rest of my answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you -- well, just to clarify that answer, what did you mean to say? You didn't say orders that I had. Did you mean to say something else?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which orders. I went out voluntarily. People were passing by, I wanted to know, wanted to see why they were leaving, what was going on, why were there columns there passing by. I spoke Albanian with them. My Albanian is as good as my Serbian, and there was no mention of any orders that I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. I think the issue has been clarified. So you told us that from the beginning or commencement of the NATO bombing campaign you began seeing this convoys of refugees passing through Decani municipality. Is this about the same time when you began seeing people in Decani municipality leave?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was happening in several instances. It wasn't just one day. You know how long the air campaign lasted. So people were not all deciding to leave on the same day. It happened throughout the air campaign. People were making their own assessments as to their safety, whether they were safe or not safe. So in several instances throughout those months, they were leaving the area, Serbs, Montenegrins and Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we can't say --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My question was a different one. You had indicated that from the beginning of the NATO bombing campaign you began seeing refugees or persons of Albanian ethnicity from other municipalities, and you've mentioned Pec as one of them crossing Decani municipality and heading to Djakovica. What I'm asking, and this is in relation to your answer where you said that it was a well known fact that Albanians and persons of other nationalities were leaving Decani, what I'm asking is whether you began seeing persons, the residents of Decani municipality leaving as well once the NATO bombing campaign began? Is that when you started noticing this happening in your own municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also then and perhaps even prior to that. Some families left the area before NATO started its air campaign. They left because of the activities of Albanian terrorists. And then later on, after the NATO campaign began they started leaving in greater numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are saying that once the NATO bombing campaign began, the inhabitants of your municipality, Decani municipality, began leaving in greater numbers; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but even before NATO bombing due to terrorist attacks and due to the fear they had for their families, they were leaving the municipality of Decani. Among them some were Albanians and some were Serbs. There were also some Albanians who were afraid of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And wouldn't you say, sir, based on your own observations on the ground that in the weeks immediately following the NATO bombing, that is the end of March, early April, do you see a larger number of persons leaving Decani municipality? You've told us that they left throughout the bombing campaign, but in this period did you see an increased number, a larger number of refugees leaving the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say that an increased number was leaving. A lot of people left even prior to that, so whoever thought of leaving had left earlier and then there was a smaller number who remained there, and eventually they left too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did persons of Albanian ethnicity leave Decani town once the NATO bombing began? Did you see that happening?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such cases, but a lot of Albanians also remained in the town of Decani in their apartments and in their houses, they remained there until KFOR arrived. They had no problem, they did not leave the area, they remained in homes and apartments without any problems. Nothing unpleasant happened to them. Nothing was done to them either by police members or by members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we've spoken about Istinic. Did you see the Albanian population or members of the Albanian population leave the village of Istinic once the NATO bombing campaign began? Did you observe that or no?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not observe that. The columns that I spoke of came from the entire territory that I mentioned. I didn't notice whether these people were from Istinic or from other place. This was the main road leading towards Djakovica and towards the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that you spoke to refugees in these columns and that they told you where they were from and the reasons why they were leaving. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did talk to them. But as for them telling me where they were from, I didn't really go into such details. I was interested in the reason for them leaving. I wasn't interested in where they hailed from, so I didn't really discuss things in detail with them. I was just inquiring about the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where is it that you had these conversations with the refugees, just on the road? You would meet them and --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I talked to them. Because the MUP building is right next to the road, so I talked to them right there by the road, by the police station in the centre of Decani.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So these columns of Albanian refugees that were coming from other municipalities and also leaving Decani, they would pass in front of the OUP building in Decani town?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was no other road. Rather, there are alternative roads via villages in Decani municipality. They could have used those roads to go to Djakovica municipality without using the main road, and then there was also a part towards Djakovica that has a split leading to Glina, so it's not like this was the only road they could have taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. So now you said you've spoken to the refugees that were passing in front of the OUP building and you have given, during your testimony, you've summarised the reasons that were given to you and your conversations as to why they were leaving the municipality. And I believe that one of the reasons that you gave yesterday and you've also repeated it today was because the NATO bombing was underway; correct? That was one of the reasons that were given to you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one of the reasons, and another important reason was that the members of the KLA --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we are going to go through the reasons, I just wanted to confirm that that was one of the reasons you had given yesterday as to why the population was leaving. Another reason you gave, and I believe that that is where you were going to as well, was that they were afraid for their lives and they were afraid for their families because of the war operations that were going on between the KLA and the MUP and they did not want to find themselves between these forces and under fire. That's at transcript page 13290. Do you recall indicating that that was another one of the reasons why they told you they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that several times already. Flyers were distributed in Albanian where the KLA was warning them that they needed to leave the area because they couldn't protect them, and they were to leave the area in order to make it seem that there was a humanitarian catastrophe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. And the third reason I was going to ... [Microphone not activated] ... mention that I believe you've already referred to, was that they had mentioned that the reason -- another reason was that the KLA was exercising pressure against them in order to create convoys and to produce some kind of humanitarian catastrophe, and that's what you were mentioning earlier, that was another reason given to you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I was just putting your testimony to you of whether that was another reason that you gave that the refugees had told you of why they were leaving, that the KLA was exercising pressure against them?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reasons for what? I have mentioned already that they were worried for their own safety, the safety of their families. They were worried about NATO bombing. They didn't want to be caught in cross-fire. They didn't want to die and lose their lives. These were all the reasons that I've mentioned a number of times in all of my statements in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to the first reason that we were discussing about NATO activity, you told us that Decani municipality was, in fact, bombed quite heavily; was that your evidence? And that created fear?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since it has a strategically important position near the border with Albania, it was quite heavily bombed especially the area next to the border and then the area within Decani itself where they bombed army members in their positions, police members. They also dropped cluster bombs in the vicinity of the Decani monastery, which is a very significant religious site that outraged Serbs and Montenegrins. They were outraged that even sacred sites in Kosovo were not protected. In addition, they also bombed factories and all vital facilities, bridges and so on. And as far as I know, they also bombed a column of civilians, Albanians, in the territory of Djakovica municipality. And this was reported by the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to the MUP being present in Decani municipality in 1998 and 1999, the VJ was also there; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no contacts whatsoever with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You did not know that there were VJ units in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew, and I would see army units, but I had no co-operation with them, no contacts, nor did we have any joint agreements or talks. Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the brigade that had responsibility for your municipality at the time, and we are speaking both in 1998 and 1999, was the 125th Motorised Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you say you saw VJ units in the municipality but you do not know which brigade these units belonged to?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can see men in uniform in town, but I didn't go as far as to talk with them or their officers. They had their job to do and I had no contacts or co-operation with them whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm not asking if you had co-operation with them. I'm just asking whether you had information of which VJ brigade had responsibility for your municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. I had no such information which brigade, what its goal was, and why it was there, just as I didn't know about their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Sir. Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to show you an exhibit, and this is P954. And it's the war diary of the 125th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I represent to you, sir, that this was the brigade which had responsibility over Decani and other areas as well, and while this is being brought up, sir, I'll already indicate to you that this is a handwritten document and so some portions of it in the photocopied Serbian version aren't as legible as in the English, so I'll be reading from the English version. If we could go to -- we see that this begins on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 in the English and also page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the entry for the 25th March. I would like to direct your attention to paragraph 1 where it says "the enemy," which I know is a bit fuzzy to read in your version. I'll read it out. It says: "During the day STS opened fire at VJ Yugoslav and MUP Ministry of the Interior units, air-raid warning signals were passed on via the reporting and early warning systems several times. There were no air attacks." Do you see that, sir? It's the first part of -- it's a bit blackened out in your version.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we go to page 5 of the English and page 6 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this is the entry for the next day, 26 March. And I'll read the second sentence, start on the second sentence. It says: "On several occasions air-raid warnings was given but NATO forces did not open fire at facilities and units in the zone of responsibility. NATO [indiscernible] high altitudes. Warning was issued that they are dropping infrared bombing markers and parachutes; if you come across them, their energy source should be removed" it says. Do you see that entry for the 26th of March? I'm just pointing to the text here.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear what you are saying, but I can't see it here in the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: At the top of the text, sir, but it is, as I said, a bit hard to read in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's illegible. It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I have pointed that out, sir, in relation to the B/C/S, that's why I'm reading from the English. I want to show you another entry, and this is page 7 of the English and page 9 in the B/C/S, and this one is also hard to read in the Serbian so I'll read out. And I draw your attention, sir, to the fact that this diary for the 27th of March, again indicates NATO forces did not attack facilities in the zone of responsibility. I do appreciate it's difficult to read in the B/C/S. And I just wanted to show you one last entry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page in the English. And we want the bottom part of that page, and it's also the next page in the B/C/S. If we could scroll down in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, for the 28th of March again, this war diary indicates NATO forces did not attack in the zone of responsibility. It is difficult to read, it's the next page in the B/C/S. Now, sir, I represent to you, sir, that the zone of responsibility of the 125th Motorised Brigade included the municipality of Decani, and according to this war diary, and I'm not going to continue going through it for the entries of the last week of March, but I put to you, sir, that they indicate that there were no NATO air attacks in their zone of responsibility, that is including in Decani. Now, sir, this is the information that the VJ, which was operating in your area had, and you are telling us that the convoys that you saw leaving Decani once the NATO bombing campaign began were leaving because of the NATO bombing, but, in fact, this diary shows that there were no NATO attacks in your area, were there, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot discuss this report. I have no idea who wrote it or how. You say that it was the army. That's the information that they had. It is their diary. According to the information and the data that I had, the situation was different. It was their zone of responsibility, they are talking about it. I don't know what their zone of responsibility was at the time. They had their own superior command and their own plans that I was never aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, sir, so you are saying you have no information about what is recorded in this diary about the fact that there were, in fact, no NATO air attacks in the zone of responsibility of the 125th, including Decani, during the last week of March? You don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that some attacks were carried out in Decani, but what the army reported or wrote, I don't know about that. That's their problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: While we are on the topic of -- and I do want to indicate that there is an air-raid recorded for the 24th of March, but it does not indicate where it occurred. That's just for reference. While we are on the topic of the NATO air-strikes, sir, yesterday you were asked whether you had any information on some inhumane measures -- if you had any information that some inhumane measures were used in your territory, and you said, yes, depleted uranium was used during the NATO bombing campaign, these were bombs that created huge craters and were very destructive. They contained depleted uranium, and this is at Transcript page 13291 and the following page. Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was happening very close to where I lived, one such bomb was dropped and the windows and the door were completely destroyed in the building, so the bomb had fallen in the vicinity of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how did you know, sir, that these bombs contained depleted uranium?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, considering the effects they produced and the depth of their craters and how destructive they were and everything else, that's how you could judge. Later on in 1999 and after the year 2000 there was a lot of talking about that, and certain areas were marked because depleted uranium had been found. It was in the media that the members of KFOR and of Italian army had had various forms of sickness caused by depleted uranium.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So this is information that you obtained after the war? The fact that these bombs contained depleted uranium is something that you learned after the war ended?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was no expert. I couldn't tell, but these were very strong detonations and the craters were large and the bombs were very destructive and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Before coming to testify here, sir, did you speak to anyone, and by anyone I mean anyone with interest in this case about the issue of depleted uranium?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that the issue surrounding the use of depleted uranium have become a live issue in this case?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you know that this topic was being discussed? That other witnesses have spoken about that in this case? Other witnesses from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not sufficiently follow what Defence witnesses testified about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that you somehow have received information that this issue is, in fact, an issue that has been discussed in this case and that that is why yesterday during the course of your testimony you mentioned this when speaking of NATO bombing? [Microphone not activated] ... you have mentioned it in order to support the Defence case on this issue, haven't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not so that I would support the Defence case, but it was really so. It was confirmed later on that depleted uranium was indeed used.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, let's move to another issue that you raised during your testimony yesterday, and this was the fact that the KLA was exercising pressure against the refugees in order to create convoys, and you said they were also distributing leaflets and they tried to spread panic among the population by using misinformation, they claimed that Serbian forces carrying out aggression against civilians in order to place that in the international media. Do you recall saying that yesterday, sir? Speaking about leaflets distributed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if we could have -- I believe you were shown one of these leaflets. This is D698.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And while that is being brought up, you said yesterday that leaflets of this kind were thrown all around in areas of Kosovo including Decani municipality and that the KLA was doing that. Do you remember saying that, sir? This is at transcript page 13292.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. It's correct that I said so yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said you had seen this earlier, this leaflet that's being displayed here?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in my area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where did you see them, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I received them from my associates in the field and also through my friends and my connections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that the MUP sometimes had the practice of distributing leaflets to the population to convey information?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which leaflets you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: For example, in 1999 weren't leaflets used by the MUP to ask Kosovo Albanians to return -- who had been displaced by fighting to return to their villages? Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, maybe to refresh your memory, I'll show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Which is P483. If we could have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, I'll just inform you that this is diplomatic correspondence from the Austrian embassy, and it's from August 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if we could go to the second page, at the bottom, in the third section.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It's a heading entitled: "IDP return - possible assistance of IC." And it says: "Text of MUP flyer in the way of its distribution not the right way to encourage the return of IDPs." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Does this refresh your recollection that the MUP sometimes distributed leaflets to convey information to the population?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I never saw anything like that, and I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back to D698. This is the leaflet in question. And we've seen it earlier on the screen, sir, and you've had the chance to look at it, and you would agree with me that it bears the stamp of the KLA but it's signed by Dr. Rugova; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says at the bottom. The president of the Kosovo Republic, Ibrahim Rugova.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree with me that propaganda is sometimes used as a tool in war?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, it was used and it is used.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we look at the leaflet, we see it's signed by Ibrahim Rugova. In this case, we have the evidence of Dr. Rugova's personal secretary, Adnan Merovci who was shown one of these leaflets, and he commented on the the leaflet, and I'll want to put to you his testimony, and this is at transcript page 2232. He was asked: "Did you have the opportunity to see any of these pamphlets that were distributed?" And he said: "I didn't see them in the act of distributing them, but I saw them in the hallway before the entrance to my flat. I saw such a pamphlet. I took a copy of it, and I saw it was mere propaganda both in terms of its contents and the way it was formulated, general layout of the pamphlet. It contained many errors, and there was a discrepancy between what it said and the insignia and the person who signed it. On top there was a KLA insignia and then signed below it was signed by Mr. Rugova when, as you well know, Mr. Rugova led the LDK and the Kosovo Liberation Army was led by other people. This shows that it was a way to strike fear and panic among the population because the text was full of mistakes in Albanian which show that it was not done by professionals and that the goal was, as I said, to strike panic among the population and to realise their aim of ethnic cleansing." And then he was asked: "And at the time did Mr. Rugova have any sort of contact with the KLA?" And he said: "No, he did not." So, sir, Mr. Merovci, who worked with Dr. Rugova at the time, told us that this was, in fact, not a leaflet that was produced by him. Do you have any comments regarding his testimony?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It would be normal for Ibrahim Rugova to say he did not do that and that he would defend himself in that way. It would not be logical for him to accept that considering the position he had as the president of the Democratic Alliance of Communists, but it is not true what he said, that he did not have any contacts with the KLA. It is correct that he did have contacts with the KLA. There were two factions in the KLA. There was Rugova's faction and there was the other one led by Bujar Bukoshi. And one more thing, I wish to say that as far as I'm familiar with the Albanian language, I don't think that there are any errors here, and I assert that this was the KLA propaganda and that they wanted to cause a humanitarian disaster and portray it, as I said earlier, as a large-scale aggression on part of the Republic of Serbia and its security forces. After that, they would also cause NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But, sir, isn't it clear from this text that, in fact, this would have been produced not by the KLA but by Serb forces because it was, in fact, Serb forces who wanted Albanians to leave Kosovo, not the KLA?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, didn't we say earlier that propaganda is used in war time? This was the propaganda used by the KLA. These were the methods that they used among their own population. Why wouldn't they use such methods when they even killed their own population?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Weren't the KLA, sir, fighting to keep control of Kosovo? Isn't that why they were fighting Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was for them to keep as much of the territory as possible, but they also wanted to abuse their own population for their own purposes, as I have said many times, so that they would bring about the NATO aggression against the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And they wanted to keep control of as much territory and that included also keep the Albanian population in Kosovo; correct? It was, in fact, Serb forces who were interested in having Albanians leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the contrary, the Serbian forces always always insisted that the Albanian civilian population should remain in their villages and in Kosovo. I'm not aware of any information that the Serbian security forces ever acted in such a manner that they would abuse the Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I see, Your Honours, it's time for the break, I'm going to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have the first break now. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, right before we broke off we were talking about the reasons for departure of the population from Decani municipality. Now, sir, in this case we have heard evidence from residents of Decani who have told us that the reason they left Decani municipality in March of 1999 was not because of the KLA bombing, or because -- of the NATO bombing or any sort of pressure from the KLA or the leaflets we've spoken about. But they said that they left the municipality because they were expelled by Serb forces and that is the police and the VJ. Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know anything about that. And I claim that this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, the evidence we have heard here is that on about the 26th of March, 1999, police arrived in the village of Drenovac and they ordered the the population to leave and the population gathered in the village of Beleg in Decani municipality. Do you know anything about that happening?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We have also heard that from refugees who were in Beleg during the last week of March then on or about the 28th of March, 1999, Serb forces arrived in large numbers and police in military vehicles to the village, that there was a large number of refugees there. They separated men and women, stripped them, searched them, and robbed them of their valuables. Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I have heard this right now from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And these witnesses have also told the Court that these forces, in fact, stayed in the village over night, that the women were taken to a separate house, and that several of them, several women and young girls were raped during the night, and that the following morning the refugees who were in Beleg were forced to leave the Serb forces by the police and the military who were there. Do you know anything about Albanian refugees being ordered to leave the village of Beleg, in Decani municipality, around the 29th of March?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no information about that case either.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, we've heard also from people who were among these refugees who were forced to leave Beleg that they were sent -- or they ended up in the village of Istinic about which we've spoken, and that they later were also forced to leave around the 1st of April, police arrived and they were forced to leave that village and they were told to head to Albania. Do you know anything about Albanian refugees being expelled from the village of Istinic around the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, we have also seen documents and evidence in this case that during these days that I've been speaking about, this is the last week of March, VJ and MUP were operating in the area of these villages. Do you know anything about VJ/MUP actions taking place in these areas, around the villages of Beleg, Istinic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any actions in that area at the time. At that time I carried out my regular duties within the OUP Decani.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know anything about a joint MUP/VJ action in the village of Kosare also in the same period?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to show you some documents, sir. Maybe this helps you with your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could please first look at P957.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this is, sir, the war diary of an armoured battalion of the 125th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this war diary covers the period from 25th March, 1999, to 16th June, 1999. I would now first like to look at page 3, both in the English and in the B/C/S. And this is the entry for the 28th of March. I'll read out a passage, which is -- we need to turn the page in the B/C/S, I see it's upside down. Thank you. It says somewhere in the top of the page: "The 1st TV" which in another -- in the earlier pages indicated means tank platoon "which had gone to Decani engaged in combat in Pozare village in order to evacuate the killed police officers, the platoon was within distance of the Novi Sad PJP. The task was not completed, one tank was hit and one soldier killed and three were seriously and slightly wounded." Does this help you, sir, with your recollection of there being an action in Pozare village in Decani around the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even in my previous testimony I said that as regards the army, their activities, their diaries, and their orders, I had nothing to do with that. I know nothing about what you are just showing me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the next page, this is page 4 in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S, 29th of March. It's again a reference to this same action in Pozare village, and I'll read our a portion. It says: "Part of the battalion consisting of seven tanks with the first infantry platoon and the 2nd Police Command Company conducted an operation to evacuate a burned-out tank and police officers killed in Pozare village. The operation was conducted successfully and the enemy suffered losses." Now, sir, we see here that this operation in Pozare village involved a large number of tanks, they are speaking about seven tanks and both a VJ and MUP unit. You are saying you had no information about this going on?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Let's look at another page, sir. This is page 6 in the English, page 6 in the B/C/S as well. This is the entry for 31st March, 1999. And I'll read out the portion of this page it says: "The preparation of five tanks for clearing up Istinic village was ordered." Do you see that on the screen, sir? Towards the middle of the page. If we could zoom in, the middle of the page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hardly legible. Its illegible, I can't see it. One can only assume what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we've spoken quite extensively or you've spoken in your testimony quite extensively about Istinic village. Do you recall anything about there being five tanks from the VJ sent to carry out clearing up tasks there on 31st March? Does that ring any bells that that happened?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that event or anything else related to MUP/VJ actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we look, sir, on the same page, just scroll down towards further down the bottom where it says: "Pec 1st April, 1999," there's a reference to the same action, this is the following day, and it says: "Four tanks within the strengths of the 2nd MTV cleared the terrain in the Istinic village sector. There were no losses or wounded." You don't recall this either, sir? On the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this all has to do with the army and the police and the MUP and the minister were responsible for the police, and I do not know about any army activities. I never co-operated with them. I wasn't informed about this. I wasn't aware about this. I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to the war diary that we were looking at earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is P954. If we could have page 12 in the B/C/S and page 10 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I put to you, sir, that this is an entry for the 28th of March, 1999 which is the week that we have been speaking about. If we look where it says 1200 hours on the top of the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I was looking for page 12 in the B/C/S, I don't believe that's at the right page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'll read out the portion, sir: "1200 hours, order sent to the commander of the brigade to provide support to MUP forces for the destruction of STS in Malisevo sector," and it has the number of the order there, and if we look at 1400 hours, 1430, it says: "PRK commander requested details in connection with operations of our unit in Decani sector and a briefing on the situation in the unit and in connection with the damaged tank." Now, sir, this war diary of the 125th seems to be indicating that this brigade was involved in joint actions with the MUP in your municipality on the 29th of March. You are telling us you had no information about this?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I know nothing about this. You are mentioning Malisevo here, and I don't know why you are mentioning that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My reference was to the second portion. I was just reading the text on the screen, sir. Sir, let me show you another document, and this is 65 ter 06099: And this is, sir, a portion of -- and I want to go to pages -- start on page 32 of the English. There's no B/C/S copy available. And this, sir, is the transcript of the testimony of the commander of the 125th Motorised Brigade in the Milutinovic case, and his name is Dragan Zivanovic, and I just want to show you what he said in relation to these events that we've been discussing, this action. I'll start reading from line 17 of this page. He is asked: "Did a clash occur in late March with the KLA forces in that area?" And this is a reference to a clash in the village of Pozare which is mentioned earlier. And he says: "On the 29th of March, we lent support to the MUP forces in the Pozare village area. We actually dispatched three tanks over there to that area. During the fighting, a tank was hit by an ambush from the rear in the Pozare village area destroying one tank and one of my soldiers were killed, Private Dunic." If we could turn the page. This witness is asked on the next page by Judge Bonomy, this is somewhere in the top of the page: "And how many troops did you engage in this?" And he says: "My two combat groups numbered 350 men. We were lending support to the MUP units and they had as many people as we did; therefore, a total of about 700 men." And Judge Bonomy asks: "How was it that you lent support to them? What did you actually do?" And the witness said: "When we say support, we mean support by manoeuvring, in this case, combat units, combat equipment, or firing. We would take up some prominent features and facilities. We would protect any advance that they made, we would secure their flanks and try to attack the firing positions of the terrorist forces wherever we believed that the MUP units alone would not have -- and we believe that the MUP units alone would not have been successful in this." Now, sir, based on the testimony of the commander of this brigade whose war diary I put to you earlier, he is indicating here that this action in Pozare village involved quite a large number of men, in fact, he refers to 700, 300 MUP, 300 VJ. And you are telling me that you heard nothing about this action taking place in Pozare village on the 29th of March?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't the person that was supposed to know. First of all, nobody had to inform me about these actions. Secondly, it was the staff and the minister that had to receive the information, so any information you need you can get from the staff and the minister. I wasn't involved neither in planning nor in implementing these actions. Here you have a member of the army. Who he reported to, I don't know. I'm also not aware of the numbers that you are putting to me here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Pozare village, sir, how far is it, if you know, from Decani town approximately?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Pozare is approximately 15 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how far is it from the village of Istinic, if you know? I'm just asking for an approximation.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like to know the distance as the crow flies or if you go by road?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just an approximation based on your knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were village roads, there were longer ones and shorter ones. I can't really claim. It depends which route one took. There were several possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were they in the same general area, Istinic, Pozare, Beleg?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not in the same general area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how far would you say that Pozare was from the village of Beleg? I'm just asking for an estimation here, sir. We have maps and we can look at them too.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that you have maps. In my estimate the distance between Pozare and Beleg, let me remember, it's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If you don't know, sir, that's okay. I don't want you to guess on this. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to 7 kilometres, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, and you are saying despite the fact this village was about 15 kilometres away from Decani and this action involved a large contingent of both VJ and MUP, you knew nothing about this happening on the 29th of March?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said this repeatedly during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've shown two pages from the transcript of commander Zivanovic, and I would like for those pages to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What were the page numbers?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: 32 and 33. And the exhibit number is 06099.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those two pages will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P01585, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, you have indicated repeatedly that you knew nothing about the expulsions and you've also told us that you knew nothing about these actions. I want to show you another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 06101. If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is a witness statement taken by the ICTY of a person, a woman by the name of Fetije Vishaj. It's dated 29th January, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like to go to page 3 in the English and page 3 also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm waiting for that, sir, to come up on the screen. So this witness tells us on page 3 that on the 28th of March, it was Bajram's Day around 11.00 in the morning in my village, which she indicates in the earlier page was Istinic, had been surrounded by Serbian army, paramilitary and police forces. All the houses from the village had been searched. There were 100 displaced persons from the village of Drenoc, Gllogjan, and Carrabreg. My house was surrounded and two policemen came into it, and later on in this statement she indicates how they were ordered to leave. Now, I want to take you to page 7 in the English and B/C/S and just to move quickly through this statement, I will represent to you, sir, that this witness ended up in the village of Beleg, and in her statement she speaks about Serb forces arriving in Beleg and speaks about women being sexually assaulted there on the night of the 28th. Now, on page 7 she is referring to events on the 29th, and in the middle of the page she says: "The next morning at 7.00, the paramilitary who took my necklace pointed his finger at me and said, 'you.' I was so frightened, then he gave me my necklace back. We were taken out. I saw and heard soldiers calling one policeman Vula. I saw him talking to soldiers. He had a white Niva car. They were always in groups. I saw Zoran," and in another place of her statement she claims that this is Zoran Djurisic together with them. "We asked them where we were being taken. They said that we would be taken to Albania. We were ordered to get on tractors, which were supposed to take us to Albania. Vula had short black hair and fat. He was the chief of police in Decani before the war." Now, sir, this witness here is placing you in Beleg at the time that she and other refugees were expelled from there. You have told us earlier today that you were, in fact, known by the nickname of Vula; correct? Do you recall anything about these events? I see that you are smiling.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that I knew why you were asking me this. The Albanians usually called me Vula because they couldn't pronounce the L sound. Now, this lady who gave this statement, I have to tell you this statement is completely incorrect. First of all, this woman doesn't even know me. Albanian women traditionally never had any contacts with police. This is a fictitious statement in which she was coached what she needed to state. This is completely untrue. Both the portions where they describe paramilitary forces and the portions concerning these events, nor do I know anything regarding these events. She describes Vula as short and fat with black hair. I'm neither short nor fat nor do I have black hair. Then she says that before the war he was chief in Decani, and I was chief during the war. So the statement is full of contradictions, imprecisions, and it is completely untrue. I see this for the first time, and all I can say is that it is not true and that I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
