utterances.text: Very well, sir, I'll move on to the testimony of another witness. Before I do that, Your Honour, can I have this statement marked for identification just for purpose of reference later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P01586 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like to bring up the transcript of transcript page 3849. This is the testimony of Mehmet Mazrekaj, and I believe the date is 28th of April, last year. If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this, sir, is a school teacher from Drenovac who testified in this case, and he was also among the civilians in Beleg who were expelled and ended up in Istinic and on the 1st of April was expelled from there. I'm going to read out a passage to you from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. It was not recorded in the transcript nor did we hear in the interpretation the first and the last name of the person giving testimony here because the witness hasn't heard that, in fact. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The person that the witness is called Mehmet Mazrekaj with a T at the end of Mehmet, Mazrekaj. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you spell the surname, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It's been -- yes, it's correct now. The first name ends with a -- yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we could look at page 3849. I'm going to read a portion of his evidence to you, sir. It starts from -- and you explain: "I know in your statement that after you escaped you eventually made your way to Isniq," which is the Albanian for Istinic. You then described the Serbs shelling Isniq. "Can you tell us when it was that Serbs shelled Isniq?" And he says: "I arrived in Isniq the following day. I remained there for two days. It was when the shelling started. There were so many people there. The whole village was filled with people. The fields around were filled with people. People from the villages of [indiscernible] municipality, they had all gathered there. The shelling was ongoing." And later he says -- he explains the position from where it was shelled and he is asked: "Can you tell us if you are aware of any interactions with the police or police authorities in Isniq? It was a huge crowd. The police in Decan issued the order to the police there that we had to leave that area. The chief of police in that area of Decan." And the transcript says "Vula." If we move on to the next page, he is asked: "Sir, can you just repeat the last name so the chief of police at the police station in Decan" - and we missed the last name - "Vukmir was his name, known as Vula, and his last name was Mircic." And it goes on to say: "Can you explain again what it was that the chief of police did?" And the person says, the witness says: "I personally did not talk to him but the villagers from Isniq and the leaders of the village told us that we had to leave the village and head towards the police -- and head towards Albania. And did the leaders of the village speak to the chief of police, is that what you are saying?" And later on if we scroll down a bit, it says: "We joined the convoy. We were told that he had instructed some leaders, some local policemen. When you say 'he' you mean the chief of police had instructed some leaders? Yes, Vula. And what did he instruct them to do? He had instructed them to tell all families there to leave the village and head towards Albania" and then he says, "everybody left towards Albania?" Sir, do you have any recollection of this of having ordered civilians who had gathered in Istinic at the beginning of April 1999 to leave and head to Albania?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement is entirely untrue, the statement by Mr. Mazrekaj. Nobody shelled the village. Nobody forced the residents to leave the village. The witness also mentions local police, and he himself was a member of local police. So by providing this statement, he wanted to safe-guard his own interests to protect himself from any repercussions by KLA and his own compatriots because he was part of the local security.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Mazrekaj was a was a school teacher from Drenovac. He was not a local police.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the local police. This is just an alibi that he wants to create for himself in order to avoid being punished or being under threat of the KLA and his compatriots. Why he is mentioning local police? Why is he mentioning that he talked to them and to me? It's not true what he is saying here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you order the refugees who had gathered in Istinic to leave the village on 1st of April and to head to Albania? Did you give that order, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not give that order. I was not present in Istinic. I did not issue any orders. This is a pure fabrication on the part of Mazrekaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, sir. This is 00473, if we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, this document that we are going to see up on the screen is an excerpt from a report published by the OSCE. It's a report called "As Seen As Told," which was published after the conflict. And this is the chapter that refers to your municipality of Decani. We see the cover page there. Have you heard of this report, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't seen this. I don't know who wrote this. I don't know what kind of a document this is. I don't know what this is about. I know -- I can see from the document that it has to do with human rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like for page 5 of the B/C/S and page 6 of the English to be shown, and I want the right side of second paragraph on both pages, if we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this is a page or a section of the report that refers to Istinic. And I'm going to just read out a portion of this page out to you, sir. It says: "On or around 1st April, Serb forces surrounded and shelled Istinic. They attacked with 13 tanks and several people were injured in the shelling. Livestock was killed, houses set on fire, and people were robbed. The Decani chief of police was present and he gave -- and gave Kosovo Albanian residents one hour to leave. Some left in cars, while others walked to the Albanian border in a convoy accompanied by police forces from Decani and also as reported from Nis. One interviewee describes how Serb boys apparently as young as 12 years old were seen in police uniforms and how stones were thrown at the Kosovo Albanian IDPs." Now, this reference to the Decani chief of police, sir, here in this report, that would be you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here commander. That's a broader term. I was chief. So it has nothing to do with me. I was not present in the village and I do not know of these events. It is not logical in an event like that to send in 10 tanks. I think this is a pure invention, and it is well known that OSCE and similar organisations looked favourably upon the KLA and frequently wrote things that were not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation, sir, as to why an organisation such as OSCE would make such an allegation in a report of this nature and indicate that the Decani chief of police was actually ordering Kosovo Albanian refugees to leave the village of Istinic? Do you have any explanation for that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have an explanation. It doesn't say chief of police in the text. It says "commander," and I don't know what commander this was. What is written here is not true. Once again I'm telling you that the OSCE and all other international organisations generally sided with the KLA and wrote things that were not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, in the English it does say Decani chief of police, so I think that's just a translation problem. And your explanation to why this allegation is being made here, sir, is that this organisation which is siding with the KLA and so that's why they have included such a specific allegation about you in their report? That is the explanation that you are giving, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all untruths, all of them. Untruths that I'm seeing for the first time. They wanted to project this image in which the Republic of Serbia was exploiting Albanians in every possible way in order to -- for the air campaign to come about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, let me show you another exhibit. Before I do that, Your Honours, could we have this exhibit marked for identification. 00473.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P01587 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like 06102 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is again a witness statement, sir, of a person called Florim Pergjagjaj, and it was taken by this Tribunal on the 6th of May, 1999. So this is immediately after the events that are described within the statement. If we could go to the next page. Now this person is also from the Decani municipality and he recounts in his statement how he was expelled from the village of Ljumbarde. It's the next page in both languages, please. I'm going to read you a portion of this statement. In the B/C/S I believe it's the next page. It's in the bottom of the English and it says: "On the 3rd of April 1999 Serb forces entered our village by several tanks and APC coloured blue. There were also green coloured tanks and APCs. Through a mega-phone Serbs ordered people to get out of their houses and leave the village. My family got into a tractor and started moving in a convoy with other people, not only from our village but also from others as well towards the town of Decan. In Decan in front of the police station, the policemen stopped every tractor and car. Almost every man would be ordered out and beaten by policemen. The other members of the family were ordered to move farther in this way, some 150 men were separated from their families. If we go to the next page he says, one man's name was Nolak [phoen] from the village of Ratic [phoen] Decan municipality. These are among the people doing the beatings who used to work as a taxi driver. A policeman called Ljubisa, son of Milos from the village of Tasenov [phoen], Decan municipality, who used to work as a policeman in the town of Jakova, two sons of Slobo Votocevic [phoen] from the village, same village also participated in the beating. And then he says: "They beat me in the presence of the chief of the Decan police department Vulio [sic] Mircic. Somebody was beating me with a rifle-butt, somebody hit me with an iron bar on the head. I tried to cover my head with my left hand, and my hand got broken as well as my middle finger on the left hands. Some of the policemen took personal documents from me. I never received them back. I received first aid only in the hospital of Kukes." Now you've told us, sir, the convoys leaving Decan would pass in front of your OUP, which was on the main road you said. Do you recall anything about this incident, sir, refugees who were leaving the municipality passing in front of your OUP and being beaten by members of the police and other Serbs in your presence?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same phenomenon like the one in the previous statements. This is not true, on the contrary. We're always there because of these refugees so we would not allow anyone to mistreat them especially if there were any Serb civilians around or any police members. This is a pure fabrication of a member of the Decani municipality who is trying in every way possible to show that the Albanian population was suffering some kind of torture. The motives are the same as those that I mentioned earlier on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I've shown you the statement of a woman who was in the village of Decan and says she saw you there when the refugees were expelled. We saw the testimony of Mr. Mazrekaj who said that you gave the order for villagers to leave Istinic. We also saw an OSCE report which has the same claim that you were the one who ordered Albanian refugees to leave Istinic and head to Albania, and now we are looking at a villager from Ljumbarda, another village in Decani who says that police -- he was forced out of the municipality right in front of your OUP, he was beaten and by police officers and other Serbs in your presence. Now, sir, can you explain why all these sources will have these allegations involving you in expulsions and mistreatment of Albanians in the period of the end of March, early April? Can you explain why it is that these different sources contain these allegations about you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's something normal. Everyone knew me. I was born in the area, so whatever untruths they wished to say and misinformation, they would connect that to me. These are all statements which they wrote on the basis of their assumption or something that somebody instructed them to do. You could have collected more than one hundred such statements that would claim one in the same thing. They were directed to talk in this way and to place all the burden on the people and the army and the police and the state and all the other organs of the Republic of Serbia so that they would represent only what is bad, what is black, not anything that is good. These statements are incorrect. I'm telling you that. They are arbitrary and they have no weight. And this is simply not true. It is a pure untruth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that the reason these different people and also the OSCE have referred to these allegations about you is because you were, in fact, not only aware that the villagers were being expelled from different villages in Decani municipality, but that you were yourself involved in these expulsions? That is the reason, sir, why these different sources all point to you.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was their goal all along. They wanted to make connections that are not true and to state allegations against certain people that are not true. I would not expect them to praise me. There are people who are praising me even among the Albanians, and they are telling the truth. These Albanians were instructed and trained to talk in this way. Somebody taught them to say something that is not true and that is unfavourable for someone else. I cannot really realise how you can conclude that there is any truth in this only on the basis of such statements. I could also tell all kinds of fabrications, but that's not real testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we have this last statement marked for identification, Your Honour, this is 06102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P01588 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, did you hear any allegations from any source that the police in your OUP were extremely violent and involved in persecutory acts against Kosovo Albanians? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not have such information nor did I hear that from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you hear any allegations that you were present when Kosovo Albanians were beaten at your police station?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an utter untruth, because I would never allow anything that was illegal to be done in my presence. Only things that were in accordance with the law could be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to show you another article, another document. And this is P1572. And this is an article from a Serbian periodical called "Nin". Have you seen this document before, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where have you seen it, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it in "Nin." Natasa Kandic wrote it as far as I can remember. It was something that wasn't true. She always dealt only in untruths and arbitrary unconfirmed data. I read it in "Nin" when I was still down there in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you saw this article when it came out in January 1999?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't remember right now, but I did read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like to go to page 3 of the English and it's also page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm going to read a passage from this article to you, sir, and it's in the bottom of the English and also in the bottom of the B/C/S. It's a paragraph beginning with a reference to Beqir Cacaj 50, from Decani. "Died on 8th June following the torture to which he was exposed to in the last days in the police station in town. Cacaj was arrested on 28th May in the time when unrests were taking place in Decani and when he was attempting to run away from the town with the rest of his family and neighbours. The following days, in several turns, he was interrogated and then brought back to the prison cell with obvious signs of torture. According to witness allegations, Vukmir Mircic, police commander in Decani police station participated in torture of Cacaj, and he hindered the transfer to the medical facility." Have you heard anything about this case, sir? About a person with the name of Beqir Cacaj being tortured at your police station? I see you are smiling.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not smiling because of such incorrect statement, I'm surprised by such articles because really the Cacajs who were living quite close to the OUP they were our good friends and neighbours, to call them that way, including Osman and everyone else. They were elderly men. So I cannot understand how anyone could write such an article, which is not true, calls me a commander, I'm not a commander. So it's clear that it's all a fabrication. It's all something that would create a bad image of the members of the Serbian MUP and the Republic of Serbia itself. It has nothing to do with what I'm testifying about here. Really, this is why I'm smiling. This is astonishing when you see something like that which is not true. And that includes many other documents which I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that you saw this article at the time, you said you remembered reading this article in "Nin". Did you inquire at the time why -- let me finish my question. At the time when you read this, did you make any inquiries as to why it was that "Nin" was publishing this sort of allegations about your OUP and about you specifically?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not because I knew all along that it was not true and that they are fabricating that. Why would I inquire? If I were inquiring, that would mean that I was believing the untruth which was published here. I would be frightened by something. I did not even pay any attention to it because I knew the real truth and it was that none of this was true. If one inquires, it means there is something about it. There's something wrong. He may have done something, and here one can see that there are some things which are really over the top. They are really over the limit, even of any untruth. Because this was a family, the Cacaj family were all my friends and neighbours, Beqir, Osman, and Suljo. I visited their house, I sat around with them. They stayed there, they remained there. Even when we left the place they stayed in their houses. So this is really an utter untruth that certain journalists and authors dealt in. You know that journalists write all kinds of things. You can put anything on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us earlier when I showed you other statements, when I put them to you, you said that these Albanians were instructed and trained to talk in that way, someone told them to say something that is not true and unfavourable for someone else. Now here we're looking at a Serbian publication, why it is that periodicals such as "Nin" would contain allegations like this about you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess you are aware that it happens today various kinds of papers publish all kinds of allegations, not just against me, but against politicians and anyone else. It's the free press, they can publish whatever they want. But I never made any conclusions on the basis of what the newspapers publish or what the journalists may decide to write.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall an inspector by the name of Zita in your OUP or known as Zita?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How did you say his name was?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Z-i-t-a. He was known by that name.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an inspector with that name. I did not have any inspectors in the civilian section of my OUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... inspectors in other sections of the police in Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inspectors were in the Djakovica SUP, also in the Pec SUP. I could have had inspectors but these working posts were never fulfilled. I did not have civilian inspectors.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to show you one last statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is 06100.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is a statement by someone called Azem Zukaj. Do you know someone by the name of Azem Zukaj, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the surname was not pronounced properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... up on the screen. It's also misspelled. It's Z-u-k-a-j.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zukaj, that's right. There were many Zukajs in the territory of the Decani municipality in several villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I believe we have the wrong exhibit on the screen. 65 ter 6100.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, this is a person from the village of Beleg in Decani municipality, and he speaks about events in 1998 and about being arrested by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Is there a problem with the exhibit? I don't see it coming up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: While that is coming up, I'll --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I see we are having a technical problem. If we could go to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I'm going read in the middle of the page. This person -- just to summarise, sir, because we can't read the whole statement. He is speaking about being detained. The next page in the -- if we could have the Serbian up. In the middle of the page he says: "I saw Vula Mircic came four times to the MUP. He would enter the room where I was and told policemen to take me to the Rugova gorge and kill me there." He also said that he had been looking for me since 1992 as I was the second Adem Jashari. He speaks about being taken there and then being brought back to the place where he was being detained, and then he says: "When Vula Mircic came for the third time, he brought the document which accused me of killing two policemen: Rade and Nikola Popovic from Sabac, Serbia. He also accused me of having a weapon without permission. He handed that document to them and they started torturing me with electric shock. I was ordered to sit on the electric chair and they would low and raise the current. They also put electric wire in my ears. It lasted for 15 minutes. This torture was too much pain, too painful. Beating was nothing compared to it." And this is an incident, sir, that takes place in June of 1998. Do you recall this, sir, being present when this person was being tortured? I see this amuses you.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person was not at the OUP at all, nor was he tortured, nor were any measures taken. Electric chair, the wires, electrical shocks, do you know what electric chair means? Nobody ever had anything like that in the Republic of Serbia. We are not criminals who did things like that, and do you know where Rugovska Klisura is located? This is a pure fabrication. He was instructed to do that so that he would accuse me because knowing me because I was born there and I lived there together with these people a long time, they wanted to connect me with these crimes to accuse me of that, but they were instructed to do that and this is done with a purpose, the taking of such statements probably with someone's assistance. This is a pure fabrication, the arrest and being brought into custody, taking him to Rugovska Klisura bringing him back, it has nothing to do with the truth. There is no Rugovska Klisura in my area. It's the first time I see this, the first time I hear about it, and I'm really surprised to see such untruths, but once again, I have to say that the untruths and lies are directed against the members of the MUP and myself and the state of Serbia, just in order to show that we are some sort of criminals, and it has nothing to do with this statement. This is really a fabrication, and it is completely untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, I've shown you over this last half an hour or so now it's been six different sources, witness statements from several different people originating from different villages, a Serbian periodical, and OSCE report, all of these sources indicate that you were involved in persecutory acts against Albanians and violence against Albanians and also expulsions of Albanians from the Decani municipality. Now, sir, why would all these different sources contain such allegations if they were not true, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not true because in that municipality it was a general practice amongst the Albanians to assign such activities to people they knew, to people who were officers or -- and this was simply with the intention to damage them or inflict them some harm. Whereas, this had nothing to do with the truth. As I told you earlier, you could have hundreds of statements of this kind because I was born in that area, I worked there, I worked there in a legal fashion, and in line with the regulations of the Republic of Serbia and the Ministry of the Interior and all of a sudden you have this scenario which leads us in an entirely different direction, and it has nothing to do with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, can you explain why it that so many different people and also OSCE and the Serbian periodical would want to fabricate things about you and damage your reputation? What would be the purpose of that, sir? Why would so many different people want to damage your reputation and make these allegations?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This didn't only have to do with me, this was a general practice in Kosovo and Metohija. They knew this they had to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I'm asking specifically about you. Why would all these different people whose evidence I've put to you and also this publication in OSCE want to damage your reputation and fabricate these sort of allegations about you. I'm speaking specifically about you. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Well, through me because they knew me as SUP chief, they wanted to paint a black picture about me and thus also about the ministry and the entire republic. So this was the core of such statements. So they didn't know any other chief because I was there, I was born there, so it was the simplest thing to say, oh, the chief was there and they quoted my name. Probably they couldn't recall any other name. And I always had very good relations with the Albanians. I was born there, I lived my entire life there as an adolescent, as a boy. And the situation which we had at that time was very different, and people were instructed, they were coached to give these kinds of statements and whoever took these statements also coached them to tell those things which were not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, isn't the real reason why all these sources speak about you in connection with these events is that it's not because they wanted to paint a black picture of you but because you were actually involved in the events that you -- that these different sources are saying that you took part in? Isn't that the real reason, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't, and it isn't true. And I can also tell you that lady Visaj, well, a woman, it is quite clear that in her statement she mentions me, she couldn't know me. It is not a tradition among the Albanian women to have any contacts with men. So it is quite clear that she was instructed to say that, and the same applies to all the other statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness. Before I conclude, I wanted to have the last exhibit 06100 MFI'd, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P01589 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Kravetz. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, we will, first of all, go back to some of the documents that were shown to you by my learned colleague Madam Kravetz during your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, if we could please see on the screen the Exhibit D107.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, you already talked about this exhibit, so this is a dispatch dated 20th of October, 1998, sent by the ministry staff, and it has to do with the decision by the minister concerning certain awards for every single day that PJP members spent in the field. You were asked some questions concerning this document. I would just like to clarify one thing. First of all, within your OUP, did you have any lists in which you would register all the members of your OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In those lists, did you also put down where these members were on a given day?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So you had the records concerning the members of OUP and PJP members when they were deployed for different tasks?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had such records but I didn't know where they went to carry out their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you informed when they came back when they were supposed to be given their regular tasks again?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And was it in line with this dispatch that you can see on the screen and the decision by the minister that we spoke about based on the number of days that they spent as members of PJP, were these people supposed to receive awards?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me, members of PJPs from your OUPs, when they were not deployed, did they carry out their regular police duties?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a difference between that and the time when they were deployed?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they were deployed as members of PJP, they carry out particular tasks in the field, so anti-terrorist actions and other security related actions in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now go back to another document that you were shown previously. It had to do with the Sat action. My question for you is as follows: Did Sat action encompass regular tasks and duties from the department of public security?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And did you participate in the implementation of that action within the remit of your regular duties?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Members of my police participated in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And did you report the SUP chief in Djakovica about this?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the Djakovica SUP chief reported to?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Djakovica SUP chief reported to the police administration at the seat of the ministry and if he deemed this to be necessary, he could have reported to the MUP staff as well, given that it existed and it had the general jurisdiction over the security in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why the police administration at the seat of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the police administration would then inform the staff about an action that was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And was the police administration in charge of the Sat action?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was exclusively the responsibility of the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you were also shown various documents, P698 and P1043, that had to do with meetings of SUP chiefs with certain persons from the staff. And I believe in one occasion, the P1043 testifies about a meeting that the minister himself also attending. Can you tell me whether you attended those meetings yourself?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never attending any of those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Certain questions were put to you concerning plans that were discussed in those meetings. Can you tell me whether at any time during the course of 1998 you yourself drafted any plans for counter-terrorist or anti-terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OUP Decani never drafted any plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see any such plans?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't involved with their drafting so I also did not have an opportunity to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what was the communication like between SUP chief and staff concerning those plans?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of today, my learned colleague showed you some statements and she also asked you why would all these persons who gave those statements say all these things about you. You also saw the statement by Mr. Mazrekaj. Do you recall that statement?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Mazrekaj was a member of the local security?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Were members of the local security faced with any problems with KLA after they signed the agreement?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the agreement they had fewer problems, but after that quite a few members of the local security were also killed, among them Elis Bajlaj, also one Cekaj and Hadajdjorno from the village of Prekoluka.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the exhibit, it used to be on 65 ter list of the Prosecution, 06100, but it has been MFI'd in the meantime, and now it's 1589 MFI. Could we please see page 2 of this document, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, so this is the person who gave the statement concerning the electric chair. You heard about this from my learned colleague. Here on page 2 in the middle of the page you can see: "My brother Skender and I were members of the KLA." Could you tell me whether members of the KLA had any motive to say things of this kind about you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, this was a general occurrence. They tried to present our work as illegal. They tried to include as many information as this in various statement and in the various media reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also you could see the book: "As Seen As Told," if I'm not mistaken, that was the title. That book was published by the Humanitarian Law Fund, Madam Natasa Kandic, the same person who, as you said, published that article in "Nin". Could you tell me whether any criminal report was ever filed against you by anybody for the allegations quoted in that article?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout my working life until the moment when I retired, I never had any criminal report or any disciplinary report or disciplinary measure instituted against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And my final question for you: In that "Nin" article, certain Mr. Zukaj answered --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cacaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Cacaj was also mentioned. Do you know what happened to that person? Was he alive at the time when you left Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were alive. This is a very respected family in Decani. They lived 100 metres away from the police station. I can mention a number of other families as well, so again, this was Natasha Kandic publishing untruths in "Nin," and I believe that she also sided with the KLA herself.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now my final question: In your testimony you said that there were also persons of Albanian nationality who could say many positive things about you, but could you tell us what is happening, are you in touch with those persons?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been in touch with many Albanians from the area of Decani up to this very day, and some of them have attempted to write a book about what truly happened there and they have asked for my assistance. So people can see that many untruthful things have been said about events in the field and that certain persons simply tried to paint the picture of Serbs as villains and criminals in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question, Mr. Mircic. Have you ever been contacted by anybody in relation to the situation in Istinic and what happened there?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never contacted by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the events of 1998 and members of the Albanian nationality. Have they ever contacted you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean later on?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later on, after everything ended the way it did?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they have contacted me. They told me that they are still grateful up to this very day about the way we organised this and how we managed to do this in this humanitarian way based on our mutual confidence and they believed that I have done a lot for the Albanians within the remit of my responsibility that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, with this I have completed my redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic. We will have the second break now and resume -- before we do, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honours, given that the Defence this morning received the Court's decision concerning the report by expert Stankovic and expert Aleksandar Pavic, I believe it might be wise in view of the decision of the counsel to postpone the Stankovic testimony until tomorrow morning. So this is our motion, and this is why I stood up before we left for the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber agrees, Mr. Djordjevic, in the circumstances, that it would be more practical not to commence the next witness today but to commence his evidence tomorrow morning so that you need not concern yourself immediately with the calling of the next witness. The Chamber, though, will now adjourn and resume at five minutes past 1.00. There may be some questions for this witness. We will have a break now and resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, I would like to get some clarifications in respect of some answers you were able to give to the Prosecution. Today, and you did that repeatedly, you stated again, "and I always had very good relations with the Albanians. I was born there, I lived my entire life there as an adolescent and as a boy." This is understandable, but can you tell me what is this source, the background of your statement, "it was the general practice amongst the Albanians to assign such activities to people they knew." You don't receive interpretation? I would like to understand your statement, "it was a general practice amongst the Albanians to assign such activities to people they knew." What is the background of this statement? How do you know that this is a general practice of the Albanians?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you had in mind the issues that pertained to me, since I used to work in the state security, I have to tell you that even before 1997 and 1998 we used to arrest a lot of persons from Decani area who had been involved in the terrorist activities, so a number of them were brought to trial and sentenced and their motive was to tell stories like that. For example, people from the families of Nazereti, Cekaj, Petolaj [phoen] and other families. So a lot of it has do with the statements that they gave. We have been working on combatting terrorism from the early 1990s, so I can tell you many facts about the persons from that area. They had family ties among them, and this in a way is their way of getting back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand that, that you are on one hand tell us that you have wonderful and good relation to the Albanians, but that you was in the position to observe that it was a general practice amongst the Albanians to assign such activities to people they knew like you. I don't understand that. Don't you see the slight contradiction?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain. Loyal Albanians, honest Albanians, Albanians who did not violate the law while I was still working in the 1980s and in the 1990s, I had no problem with them. And this does not pertain just to Albanians, it pertains to Serbs as well. You know that the police everywhere in the world works in accordance with the law, with the rules of service, with the constitution and so on, so at that time we worked out in the ground in Decani municipality, and there were a lot of illegal groups active in that area. In 1995 and in 1996 there were numerous attacks on the branch station in Rznic, terrorist attacks using mortars, hand-grenades, and other weaponry, so we had to undertake measures against these people. We had to identify them, we had to use certain repressive measures to bring them in, to bring them to trial. And the Albanians have very close links between them, so if there are any family ties by marriage or blood ties, you automatically spread that opinion among everybody in your family. And that did not concern only me. It also concerned my colleagues Albanians who used to work with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that you are not only referring to Albanians but to Serbs as well? Because you were referring to a practice in every country of the world where the police has a certain task, this is not always popular. Do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me give you an example. For example, by detaining Jovanovic who had committed a grave murder by killing four persons in Decani, that alone, by doing that alone I created a lot of enemies. People were angry that I didn't conceal that. Why didn't I conceal that murder? And the man had killed four Albanians, two couples. So there's now a whole group of Serbs who hate me for that, Serbs who have family ties to the man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I understand that, but why did you say this morning it was a general practice amongst the Albanians to assign such activities to people they knew? You were only referring to Albanians but now I understood your answer.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, because we took certain measures. We arrested people in 1980s, and 1990s. My area was quite active when it comes to security issues. They were spreading flyers, they were writing slogans and graffiti. They were infiltrating illegal groups from Albania, and we acted against those people, and all of these families were from the area of Decani municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question. The Prosecution has put a lot of previous statements of different people to you this morning, and you repeatedly said they were instructed to give these statements. What do you mean with they were instructed? Who did instruct them? Could you explain that a little bit further, please.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you just take the statements that I saw as an example, from those families, there were members that we used to arrest in the 1980s, and 1990s, people who had participated in demonstrations, who were members of terrorist groups. For example, Mazrekaj has 500 people in their family, 500 family members and some other family may have 200 members, and one of these women who gave a statement, Visaj, she could not have given that kind of a statement on her own. She is illiterate. Somebody coached her how she should phrase her statement, how she should describe me so that I could be described in that statement. Why was there nothing true in that statement. Maybe if there were people from Istinic who could have given you a different story, who could have told you about how we helped them, how we helped them by confiscating weapons in that family, and that would have been a positive example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, I take it from your answer that you are referring to the families of those people who gave these statements? They were instructed by their families; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the families, the families coached them to do this due to some earlier police action against those families. So this would be a kind of a revenge on their part. You know, that the police, the judiciary, and the prosecutor's work, none of us are really popular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, I direct your mind to the evidence you gave as respect to the OSCE. Now, you said you had good co-operation with all the verifiers who came to see you and you always had good discussions with them, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a correct attitude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. You also stated though that you had information that the verifiers were biased in favour of the KLA -- sorry -- shall I repeat that for you? Shall I repeat that for you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: The verifiers were biased in favour of the KLA terrorist groups, and you had confirmed information that they provided the KLA with information about your forces and positions and you said, well, in a way they were providing logistical support to the KLA. Yes?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: But tell me, did you ever confront the OSCE authorities with this information? Did you ever go to them and say, look here, you know, your people on the ground, you know, they're been biased, they aren't performing according to the mandate? Did you complain to the authorities of the OSCE about that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my contacts with OSCE and my contacts with them were extremely good, and they were always in accordance with the instructions we received from the ministry. I was always very correct. I provided them all of the information that they were interested in. However, they abused our assistance and the information they received from us, and they portrayed things differently than they should have realistically. In the village of Jablanica where Ramush Haradinaj was and the mere contact that the OSCE had with Ramush Haradinaj was sufficient enough to make certain conclusions, and I had verified information that they were providing to Ramush Haradinaj information about our forces, the disposition of our forces on the like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Splendid. But my question to you is, having received this information, you are now in possession of information that the verifiers are acting in a biased manner. They are -- they are not carrying out the mandate. Did you complain to the OSCE authorities about that ever?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My job was to write a report and to send it to the chief of the secretariat of the Djakovica SUP. That was my task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Do you know whether a complaint was ever lodged with the OSCE authorities on this matter at all?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, but I did inform the chief of the secretariat, and I don't know what he did in turn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also said on the question of the OSCE, you said that you followed through an instructional dispatch on how to treat OSCE members on their diplomatic status, on the necessity to treat them fairly and to provide them with the conditions necessary for their work.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would have done it even without any instructions, I'm simply such a man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Splendid. Splendid. Did you ever require the OSCE members to give you advance notice if they wanted to carry out an inspection?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. If they thought it necessary, they could have come to see me, but they also could have gone somewhere without me knowing about that. They did not need to ask any sort of consent from me in order to carry out an inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very of much. And one last question, Mr. Mircic. Now, you said that depleted uranium was used during the NATO campaign, didn't you? You said that the bombs were very destructive?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Were the population told about the depleted uranium at the time of the bombing?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, misinformation was circulated in the media, however, it was not confirmed. However, after 2000 and nowadays, many things, many pieces of information are being confirmed about the use of depleted uranium at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: So at the time of the actual bombing, there was no confirmed information as respects depleted uranium?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, but I'm not an expert. I didn't hear anybody confirming anything, but they are confirming it now. The sources from Kosovo and Metohija and many experts there are now saying that depleted uranium was used there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, I thank you very much indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That completes the questions for you, Mr. Mircic. I would like to thank you for your attendance here and for the assistance you have been able to give. You may now, of course, return to your normal activities, and a Court Officer will show you from the court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any matter that needs to be dealt with at this point before we adjourn? Ms. Kravetz? Mr. Djordjevic or Mr. Popovic? Very well, we will adjourn then and resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
